source.description: The attacker-controlled instruction bytes are read/parsed by cs_disasm(Data+1, Size-1, ...); this disassembler parse call is the scored source rather than the libFuzzer callback.
source.value_from: PoC instruction bytes are read/parsed by the Capstone disassembler.; value `Data+1/Size-1`; from `size_t count = cs_disasm(handle, Data+1, Size-1, address, 0, &all_insn);`

sink.description: MSan reports use-of-uninitialized-value when printOperand branches on/reads MI->op1_size.

root_cause.description: BND memory opcodes were missing from the switch that initializes MI->x86opsize before printMemReference copies it into MI->op1_size.

tainted_value_origin.code: r = handle->disasm(ud, buffer, size, &mci, &insn_size, offset, handle->getinsn_info);
tainted_value_origin.description: The selected architecture decoder materializes instruction operands/opcode state into MCInst mci from attacker-controlled bytes.

coarse_trace.summary: Parses attacker-controlled instruction bytes with Capstone.
Decodes bytes into MCInst and calls the X86 printer.
Generated asm writer dispatches to memory operand printing for the decoded BND instruction.
Missing BND opcode cases leave MI->x86opsize uninitialized for the memory operand path.
Reads MI->op1_size, matching the MSan crash location.

fine_trace.code: size_t count = cs_disasm(handle, Data+1, Size-1, address, 0, &all_insn);
fine_trace.note: Scored source: cs_disasm reads/parses attacker-controlled instruction bytes from Data+1/Size-1 into Capstone decoding.

fine_trace.code: r = handle->disasm(ud, buffer, size, &mci, &insn_size, offset, handle->getinsn_info);
fine_trace.note: The architecture decoder interprets attacker-controlled bytes and fills MCInst fields including the opcode that selects the generated print path.
The decoded instruction is passed to the X86 Intel printer; this frame is in the MSan stack.
Generated X86 writer dispatches BND memory operands to printanymem, where the missing BND cases fail to initialize MI->x86opsize.
In the vulnerable version the switch lacks BNDCL/BNDCN/BNDCU/BNDSTX/BNDLDX cases, so MI->x86opsize is not initialized for those memory opcodes. The patch adds those cases with sizes 4 or 8.
MSan origin stack points here: the uninitialized x86opsize value is copied into op1_size.
The printer continues and later reaches printOperand with the same MCInst state.
MSan crash_location reports use of the uninitialized op1_size value at this branch.
